_doc: Per-agent model routing (mission 2026-07-05). Two layers, honestly separated: (1) claudeTier = the Claude model the subagent RUNS on (Agent-tool `model` param; aligns with FORGE_MODEL_ROUTING.json); (2) nvidia = which NVIDIA role-model (from model-capability-matrix.json roles) the agent calls AS A TOOL (via forge-bin/nvidia-provider.cjs) for LLM-work inside its task — drafts, summaries, classification, bulk generation, second-opinion review, vision. Claude-FIRST is the default (see usagePolicy below): NVIDIA is bulk-offload-only and is HARD-BLOCKED in code for the claudeWinsSkipNvidia Bosses; premium stays premium — never silently downgrade the premium/claude layer because an NVIDIA model exists. If NVIDIA is down/no-key/unsuitable → fallbackBehavior.
fallbackBehavior: Adapter without key or on repeated failure → mock/off mode; the agent simply does the work itself on its Claude runtime model (labeled 'nvidia-skipped'). Never fake an NVIDIA response; never block work because NVIDIA is unavailable.

usagePolicy._verdict: NVIDIA-as-tool is BULK-OFFLOAD-ONLY (evidence: NVIDIA-vs-Claude comparison 2026-07-07). The Claude subagent is ALREADY running, so calling NVIDIA only pays off when it offloads genuinely BULK, LOW-RISK, high-volume output on a SEPARATE budget — never for quality-critical work. Default posture = Claude does it itself (nvidia-skipped).

claudeWinsSkipNvidia.why: Reasoning/planning: Opus 4.8 is #1 (HLE 49.8% vs kimi 36.4%). Review: Opus 88.6% SWE-Verified / 69.2% SWE-Pro, ~4x fewer missed flaws vs mistral-large-3 (mid-tier). Security/integration: high-risk, errors costly. Vision: adapter is text-only + Claude leads OSWorld. For all these, Claude already-running is better AND cheaper (no extra hop) → skip NVIDIA.

nvidiaForBulkOnly.why: NVIDIA earns its place ONLY on bulk sub-tasks: first-draft docs, metadata/audit first-pass, source pre-summarization, registry/mapping validation, bulk test-fixture generation, and mechanical scaffolding/CRUD/DTO codegen — always on a separate budget and, for any code, behind the mandatory Forge build+test verification gate. The substantive part of each role still runs on Claude.

usagePolicy.codingNote: Claude Sonnet 5/Opus 4.8 (77-82% SWE-Verified) >> gpt-oss-120b (62.4%). Real implementation/refactors/hard bugs stay on Claude; gpt-oss-120b only for mechanical high-volume codegen behind the build+test gate.

boss.why: Orchestration is highest-stakes → ALWAYS Opus 4.8 runtime (user rule). NVIDIA is only a light in-task tool (fast working model) for long-context digestion/summaries; the slow 'reasoning' (Ultra) model would stall the Lead.

head-chef.why: Task DECOMPOSITION benefits from strong reasoning → kimi-k2.6 (best working single-shot reasoner). The Boss/Opus still owns deep MISSION planning; escalate runtime to Opus on complex missions.

review-boss.why: Final QA must be strong (user rule: no weak cheap model). NVIDIA review model only as an EXTRA second opinion, never the sole verdict.

test-boss.why: Test planning/generation is coding work; Playwright execution is tooling, not model.

ui-boss.fallbackNote: NVIDIA vision is NOT usable today: the adapter sends TEXT ONLY (no image blocks) and the live multimodal models (qwen3.5-397b/122b) hang. So UI Boss's real screenshot/image analysis runs on its CLAUDE runtime (Sonnet/Opus receive images via the Agent tool). NVIDIA may still do TEXT-only UI reasoning via 'default'. Revisit when the adapter gains image support + a non-hanging vision model.
ui-boss.why: Screenshot/UI analysis needs images → Claude runtime (which gets them); NVIDIA text-only otherwise.

seo-boss.why: Structured audit work — solid general model, not creative-only.

security-boss.why: Security is high risk → Opus runtime (hardTasksAlwaysOpus); NVIDIA only as an extra reasoning lens (kimi-k2.6, best working reasoner — sharp on code-security in probe), never the sole verdict. The live safety sidecar nvidia/nemotron-content-safety-reasoning-4b may classify jailbreak/unsafe-content but is NOT the code-security judge.

search-boss.why: Source-grounded research; real search tools do the finding, model does synthesis.

build-boss.why: Implementation → coding-capable models only (user rule) — fallback stays coding-capable too; escalate runtime to Opus on hard/multi-file work (Boss decides).

integration-boss.why: API/auth/error-handling architecture; escalate to Opus for auth/data-model work (mandatory per FORGE_MODEL_ROUTING).

docs-boss.why: Docs are cheap/fast work — unless complex architecture/security content, then Sonnet runtime.

validation: Before dispatch: warn/block when an agent's assigned model violates 'prohibited' or the task clearly exceeds the model's caps (e.g. vision task on a non-vision model, implementation on a non-coding model). The adapter's `route <agent>` command resolves + validates this map against the capability matrix.
_effortNote: claudeEffort (2026-07-12, video-research verified): documentation MIRROR of the native `effort:` frontmatter in .claude/agents/<boss>.md (second routing axis: reasoning depth per Boss, on top of model tier). Source of truth = the agent file; this field only keeps routing readable in one place. Set only where beneficial: review/security xhigh (deep QA/audit), boss/head-chef high (mission/decomposition). Haiku-routed Bosses deliberately have NO effort line (unsupported levels silently fall back); NVIDIA-as-tool routing is unaffected.
